12:27 Coy is trying too hard to defend it. Great storytelling is great storytelling no matter the medium. Was it underwhelming? Definitely. It didn’t have to be an apocalypse level kind of thing, but simple writing, do the things you say your story and your characters are going to do, if you can’t and choose to go in another direction, all it would take is one or a few lines to address it. For me, this show has been doing a rinse and repeat since S2, just so they could get to their season 5. If your story cannot justify or answer questions on the actions taken by your characters, then obviously you have failed. If the decisions made by your characters are not within character, do not make sense for the story being told in the moment and only serve to set up a future narrative, then you have failed. There are much better shows out there that were told without the need of big battle scenes and it made sense for the story. And if you are saying, it was all in service of the characters, not necessarily the narrative, then I point you to shows that are much better character pieces than whatever that finale was trying to be: The Penguin, Peacemaker S1&2

The 2 big Homelander fights in Season 3, the fight scene with Deep and Black Noir in the building (for season 4 I think), and now the finale, all took place in one small room, and with none of those fights, does keeping it contained to one room, make any logical sense. I like action, but yeah that's not what the show really is. It's emotional and character driven. The plot of the show took so many hits because of all the character work through out the entirety of it's run, and then these big action moments, where a lot of emotional payoff has been fitted into them, make no sense. Somebody as strong and fast as Homelander, for one, should have been able to fly away, but he absolutely should have been tossing Butcher and Kimiko through walls, or up in the air, or something like that. Like instead of Kimiko just standing there like open, mouthed Pikachu; what if Kimiko had that vision of Frenchie while her body is healing and unliquifying, because Homelander dropped her onto the ground from the highest point of Earth's atmosphere? Idk. I'm not upset because of just the smaller scale; I'm upset because the scale makes no sense. Homelander, the main objective of the show, when he wasn't the star of the show, was absolutely nerfed for the finale, even though he just got a power up. When the big bad powerful threat, who IS supposed to be the strongest manchild in a world full of superpowered individuals, WHO IS SUPPOSED TO BE THAT POWERFUL, was handled like almost any other fight in the show. The fact that Homelander was absolutely supposed to be the threat of all threats in the show, didn't feel that strong. If they beat up on Homelander with just 3 people, after he just got a power up, WHY TF DID IT TAKE 5 SEASONS TO KILL HIM? The show probably could have been over by season 3. Since then, the show has felt like it's just been on just to keep going on. The Gen V inclusion, with no actual plan to incorporate them, probably rubbed people the wrong way; especially because people like me, thought I stupidly had to do homework to stay in the loop, and I 1,000% didn't have to do that. People are mad because the show was absolutely mishandled in many ways, while also doing some things really great. My main problem with the show: he's a great character, but Homelander literally stole too much screen time.
